ec2.DescribeAddresses.doc: Describes the specified Elastic IP addresses or all of your Elastic IP addresses.

Addresses.doc: Information about the Elastic IP addresses.

AssociationId.doc: The ID representing the association of the address with an instance.

NetworkInterfaceId.doc: The ID of the network interface.

NetworkInterfaceOwnerId.doc: The ID of the Amazon Web Services account that owns the network interface.

PrivateIpAddress.doc: The private IP address associated with the Elastic IP address.

Tags.doc: Any tags assigned to the Elastic IP address.

Value.doc: The value of the tag. Constraints: Tag values are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 256 Unicode characters.

InstanceId.doc: The ID of the instance that the address is associated with (if any).

ClientVpnEndpoints.doc: Information about the Client VPN endpoints.

ClientVpnEndpointId.doc: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint.

Description.doc: A brief description of the endpoint.

Status.doc: The current state of the Client VPN endpoint.

Code.doc: The state of the Client VPN endpoint. Possible states include: pending-associate - The Client VPN endpoint has been created but no target networks have been associated. CreationTime.doc: The date and time the Client VPN endpoint was created.

DeletionTime.doc: The date and time the Client VPN endpoint was deleted, if applicable.

DnsName.doc: The DNS name to be used by clients when connecting to the Client VPN endpoint.

ClientCidrBlock.doc: The IPv4 address range, in CIDR notation, from which client IP addresses are assigned.

DnsServers.doc: Information about the DNS servers to be used for DNS resolution.

SplitTunnel.doc: Indicates whether split-tunnel is enabled in the Client VPN endpoint. For information about split-tunnel VPN endpoints, see Split-Tunnel Client VPN endpoint in the Client VPN Administrator Guide .

VpnProtocol.doc: The protocol used by the VPN session.

TransportProtocol.doc: The transport protocol used by the Client VPN endpoint.

VpnPort.doc: The port number for the Client VPN endpoint.

AssociatedTargetNetworks.doc: Information about the associated target networks. A target network is a subnet in a VPC.

item.doc: Describes a target network that is associated with a Client VPN endpoint. A target network is a subnet in a VPC.

ServerCertificateArn.doc: The ARN of the server certificate.

AuthenticationOptions.doc: Information about the authentication method used by the Client VPN endpoint.

item.doc: Describes the authentication methods used by a Client VPN endpoint. For more information, see Authentication in the Client VPN Administrator Guide .

ActiveDirectory.doc: Information about the Active Directory, if applicable.

DirectoryId.doc: The ID of the Active Directory used for authentication.

MutualAuthentication.doc: Information about the authentication certificates, if applicable.

ClientRootCertificateChain.doc: The ARN of the client certificate.

FederatedAuthentication.doc: Information about the IAM SAML identity provider, if applicable.

SamlProviderArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM SAML identity provider.

SelfServiceSamlProviderArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM SAML identity provider for the self-service portal.

ConnectionLogOptions.doc: Information about the client connection logging options for the Client VPN endpoint.

Enabled.doc: Indicates whether client connection logging is enabled for the Client VPN endpoint.

CloudwatchLogGroup.doc: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group to which connection logging data is published.

CloudwatchLogStream.doc: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log stream to which connection logging data is published.

Tags.doc: Any tags assigned to the Client VPN endpoint.

Key.doc: The key of the tag. Constraints: Tag keys are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 127 Unicode characters. May not begin with aws: .

Value.doc: The value of the tag. Constraints: Tag values are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 256 Unicode characters.

SecurityGroupIds.doc: The IDs of the security groups for the target network.

SelfServicePortalUrl.doc: The URL of the self-service portal.

ClientConnectOptions.doc: The options for managing connection authorization for new client connections.

Enabled.doc: Indicates whether client connect options are enabled.

LambdaFunctionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function used for connection authorization.

Status.doc: The status of any updates to the client connect options.

SessionTimeoutHours.doc: The maximum VPN session duration time in hours. Valid values: 8 | 10 | 12 | 24 Default value: 24

Enabled.doc: Current state of text banner feature. Valid values: true | false

BannerText.doc: Customizable text that will be displayed in a banner on Amazon Web Services provided clients when a VPN session is established. UTF-8 encoded characters only. Maximum of 1400 characters.

DisconnectOnSessionTimeout.doc: Indicates whether the client VPN session is disconnected after the maximum sessionTimeoutHours is reached. If true , users are prompted to reconnect client VPN. If false , client VPN attempts to reconnect automatically. The default value is false .

If OutsideIpAddressType in your VPN connection options is set to PrivateIpv4 , you can use an RFC6598 or RFC1918 private IPv4 address. If OutsideIpAddressType is set to PublicIpv4 , you can use a public IPv4 address.

CreationTime.doc: The date and time the flow log was created.

DeliverLogsErrorMessage.doc: Information about the error that occurred. Rate limited indicates that CloudWatch Logs throttling has been applied for one or more network interfaces, or that you've reached the limit on the number of log groups that you can create. Access error indicates that the IAM role associated with the flow log does not have sufficient permissions to publish to CloudWatch Logs. Unknown error indicates an internal error.

ResourceId.doc: The ID of the resource being monitored.

LogFormat.doc: The format of the flow log record.

Tags.doc: The tags for the flow log.

Value.doc: The value of the tag. Constraints: Tag values are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 256 Unicode characters.

MaxAggregationInterval.doc: The maximum interval of time, in seconds, during which a flow of packets is captured and aggregated into a flow log record. When a network interface is attached to a Nitro-based instance , the aggregation interval is always 60 seconds (1 minute) or less, regardless of the specified value. Valid Values: 60 | 600

FileFormat.doc: The format for the flow log.

HiveCompatiblePartitions.doc: Indicates whether to use Hive-compatible prefixes for flow logs stored in Amazon S3.

PerHourPartition.doc: Indicates whether to partition the flow log per hour.

NextToken.doc: The token to request the next page of items. This value is null when there are no more items to return.

ec2.DescribeImages.doc: Describes the specified images (AMIs, AKIs, and ARIs) available to you or all of the images available to you. The images available to you include public images, private images that you own, and private images owned by other Amazon Web Services accounts for which you have explicit launch permissions. Recently deregistered images appear in the returned results for a short interval and then return empty results. After all instances that reference a deregistered AMI are terminated, specifying the ID of the image will eventually return an error indicating that the AMI ID cannot be found. When Allowed AMIs is set to enabled , only allowed images are returned in the results, with the imageAllowed field set to true for each image. In audit-mode , the imageAllowed field is set to true for images that meet the account's Allowed AMIs criteria, and false for images that don't meet the criteria. For more information, see EnableAllowedImagesSettings . We strongly recommend using only paginated requests. Unpaginated requests are susceptible to throttling and timeouts. UsageOperation.doc: The operation of the Amazon EC2 instance and the billing code that is associated with the AMI. usageOperation corresponds to the lineitem/Operation column on your Amazon Web Services Cost and Usage Report and in the Amazon Web Services Price List API . You can view these fields on the Instances or AMIs pages in the Amazon EC2 console, or in the responses that are returned by the DescribeImages command in the Amazon EC2 API, or the describe-images command in the CLI.

Ebs.doc: Parameters used to automatically set up EBS volumes when the instance is launched.

DeleteOnTermination.doc: Indicates whether the EBS volume is deleted on instance termination. For more information, see Preserving Amazon EBS volumes on instance termination in the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

Iops.doc: The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS). For gp3 , io1 , and io2 volumes, this represents the number of IOPS that are provisioned for the volume. For gp2 volumes, this represents the baseline performance of the volume and the rate at which the volume accumulates I/O credits for bursting. The following are the supported values for each volume type: gp3 : 3,000 - 16,000 IOPS io1 : 100 - 64,000 IOPS io2 : 100 - 256,000 IOPS For io2 volumes, you can achieve up to 256,000 IOPS on instances bu…

You can specify a volume size that is equal to or larger than the snapshot size. The following are the supported sizes for each volume type: gp2 and gp3 : 1 - 16,384 GiB io1 : 4 - 16,384 GiB io2 : 4 - 65,536 GiB st1 and sc1 : 125 - 16,384 GiB standard : 1 - 1024 GiB

Throughput.doc: The throughput that the volume supports, in MiB/s. This parameter is valid only for gp3 volumes. Valid Range: Minimum value of 125. Maximum value of 1000.

OutpostArn.doc: The ARN of the Outpost on which the snapshot is stored. This parameter is not supported when using CreateImage .

The effect of setting the encryption state to true depends on the volume origin (new or from a snapshot), starting encryption state, ownership, and whether encryption by default is enabled. After you connect to the instance, you must mount the volume. NVMe instance store volumes are automatically enumerated and assigned a device name. Value.doc: The value of the tag. Constraints: Tag values are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 256 Unicode characters.

VirtualizationType.doc: The type of virtualization of the AMI.

BootMode.doc: The boot mode of the image. For more information, see Boot modes in the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

TpmSupport.doc: If the image is configured for NitroTPM support, the value is v2.0 . For more information, see NitroTPM in the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

DeprecationTime.doc: The date and time to deprecate the AMI, in UTC, in the following format: YYYY - MM - DD T HH : MM : SS Z. If you specified a value for seconds, Amazon EC2 rounds the seconds to the nearest minute.

ImdsSupport.doc: If v2.0 , it indicates that IMDSv2 is specified in the AMI. DeregistrationProtection.doc: Indicates whether deregistration protection is enabled for the AMI.

LastLaunchedTime.doc: The date and time, in ISO 8601 date-time format , when the AMI was last used to launch an EC2 instance. When the AMI is used to launch an instance, there is a 24-hour delay before that usage is reported. lastLaunchedTime data is available starting April 2017.

ImageAllowed.doc: If true , the AMI satisfies the criteria for Allowed AMIs and can be discovered and used in the account. If false and Allowed AMIs is set to enabled , the AMI can't be discovered or used in the account. If false and Allowed AMIs is set to audit-mode , the AMI can be discovered and used in the account. For more information, see Control the discovery and use of AMIs in Amazon EC2 with Allowed AMIs in Amazon EC2 User Guide .

SourceImageId.doc: The ID of the source AMI from which the AMI was created. The ID only appears if the AMI was created using CreateImage , CopyImage , or CreateRestoreImageTask . The ID does not appear if the AMI was created using any other API. For some older AMIs, the ID might not be available. For more information, see Identify the source AMI used to create a new AMI in the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

For more information, see Identify the source AMI used to create a new AMI in the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

ec2.DescribeInstances.doc: Describes the specified instances or all instances. If you specify instance IDs, the output includes information for only the specified instances. If you specify filters, the output includes information for only those instances that meet the filter criteria. If you do not specify instance IDs or filters, the output includes information for all instances, which can affect performance. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully. If you specify an instance ID that is not valid, an error is returned. If you specify an instance that you do not own, it is not included in the output. Recently terminated instances might appear in the returned results. This interval is usually less than one hour. If you describe instances in the rare case where an Availability Zone is experiencing a service disruption and you specify instance IDs that are in the affected zone, or do not specify any instance IDs at all, the call fails. If you describe instances and specify only instance IDs that are in an unaffected zone, the call works normally. We strongly recommend using only paginated requests. ec2.DescribeVpnConnections.doc: Describes one or more of your VPN connections. For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide .

VpnConnections.doc: Information about one or more VPN connections.

Category.doc: The category of the VPN connection. A value of VPN indicates an Amazon Web Services VPN connection. A value of VPN-Classic indicates an Amazon Web Services Classic VPN connection.

TransitGatewayId.doc: The ID of the transit gateway associated with the VPN connection.

CoreNetworkArn.doc: The ARN of the core network.

CoreNetworkAttachmentArn.doc: The ARN of the core network attachment.

GatewayAssociationState.doc: The current state of the gateway association.

EnableAcceleration.doc: Indicates whether acceleration is enabled for the VPN connection.

StaticRoutesOnly.doc: Indicates whether the VPN connection uses static routes only. Static routes must be used for devices that don't support BGP.

LocalIpv4NetworkCidr.doc: The IPv4 CIDR on the customer gateway (on-premises) side of the VPN connection.

RemoteIpv4NetworkCidr.doc: The IPv4 CIDR on the Amazon Web Services side of the VPN connection.

LocalIpv6NetworkCidr.doc: The IPv6 CIDR on the customer gateway (on-premises) side of the VPN connection.

RemoteIpv6NetworkCidr.doc: The IPv6 CIDR on the Amazon Web Services side of the VPN connection.

OutsideIpAddressType.doc: The type of IPv4 address assigned to the outside interface of the customer gateway. Valid values: PrivateIpv4 | PublicIpv4 Default: PublicIpv4

TransportTransitGatewayAttachmentId.doc: The transit gateway attachment ID in use for the VPN tunnel.

TunnelInsideIpVersion.doc: Indicates whether the VPN tunnels process IPv4 or IPv6 traffic.

OutsideIpAddress.doc: The external IP address of the VPN tunnel.

TunnelInsideCidr.doc: The range of inside IPv4 addresses for the tunnel.

TunnelInsideIpv6Cidr.doc: The range of inside IPv6 addresses for the tunnel.

PreSharedKey.doc: The pre-shared key (PSK) to establish initial authentication between the virtual private gateway and the customer gateway.

Phase1LifetimeSeconds.doc: The lifetime for phase 1 of the IKE negotiation, in seconds.

Phase2LifetimeSeconds.doc: The lifetime for phase 2 of the IKE negotiation, in seconds.

RekeyMarginTimeSeconds.doc: The margin time, in seconds, before the phase 2 lifetime expires, during which the Amazon Web Services side of the VPN connection performs an IKE rekey.

RekeyFuzzPercentage.doc: The percentage of the rekey window determined by RekeyMarginTimeSeconds during which the rekey time is randomly selected.

ReplayWindowSize.doc: The number of packets in an IKE replay window.

DpdTimeoutSeconds.doc: The number of seconds after which a DPD timeout occurs.

DpdTimeoutAction.doc: The action to take after a DPD timeout occurs.

item.doc: The Diffie-Hellmann group number for phase 2 IKE negotiations.

Value.doc: The Diffie-Hellmann group number.

IkeVersions.doc: The IKE versions that are permitted for the VPN tunnel.

item.doc: The internet key exchange (IKE) version permitted for the VPN tunnel.

Value.doc: The IKE version.

StartupAction.doc: The action to take when the establishing the VPN tunnels for a VPN connection.

LogOptions.doc: Options for logging VPN tunnel activity.

CloudWatchLogOptions.doc: Options for sending VPN tunnel logs to CloudWatch.

LogEnabled.doc: Status of VPN tunnel logging feature. Default value is False . Valid values: True | False

LogGroupArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudWatch log group to send logs to.

LogOutputFormat.doc: Configured log format. Default format is json . Valid values: json | text

EnableTunnelLifecycleControl.doc: Status of tunnel endpoint lifecycle control feature.

Routes.doc: The static routes associated with the VPN connection.

DestinationCidrBlock.doc: The CIDR block associated with the local subnet of the customer data center.

Source.doc: Indicates how the routes were provided.

State.doc: The current state of the static route.

Value.doc: The value of the tag. Constraints: Tag values are case-sensitive and accept a maximum of 256 Unicode characters.

item.doc: Describes telemetry for a VPN tunnel.

LastStatusChange.doc: The date and time of the last change in status. This field is updated when changes in IKE (Phase 1), IPSec (Phase 2), or BGP status are detected.

OutsideIpAddress.doc: The Internet-routable IP address of the virtual private gateway's outside interface.

Status.doc: The status of the VPN tunnel.

StatusMessage.doc: If an error occurs, a description of the error.

CertificateArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPN tunnel endpoint certificate.

VpnConnectionId.doc: The ID of the VPN connection.

State.doc: The current state of the VPN connection.

CustomerGatewayConfiguration.doc: The configuration information for the VPN connection's customer gateway (in the native XML format). CustomerGatewayId.doc: The ID of the customer gateway at your end of the VPN connection.

VpnGatewayId.doc: The ID of the virtual private gateway at the Amazon Web Services side of the VPN connection.

ec2.DescribeVpnGateways.doc: Describes one or more of your virtual private gateways. For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide .

VpnGateways.doc: Information about one or more virtual private gateways.

SerialConsoleAccessEnabled.doc: If true , access to the EC2 serial console of all instances is enabled for your account. If false , access to the EC2 serial console of all instances is disabled for your account.

ManagedBy.doc: The entity that manages access to the serial console. Possible values include: account - Access is managed by the account. declarative-policy - Access is managed by a declarative policy and can't be modified by the account.
